findings.title: Wake coalescing flag can stay stuck and stop all future refreshes
findings.message: `pending` is set to true before the custom event is sent. It is only reset inside the Scene handler. If the event is dropped (full queue, a window not yet or no longer receiving it, or the handler's type assertion failing), `pending` stays true. Every later `wake()` is then a no-op and the UI stops refreshing for the rest of the run.
findings.suggestion: Reset `pending` when the send cannot be confirmed, for example by clearing it on the wake-event handler's early-return paths and in `OnClose`. Alternatively, drop the coalescing flag and always send, letting `a.Drain()` and `TakeDirty` deduplicate.

finding.title: Compiled binary committed to the repository
finding.message: A compiled executable is committed to the repository. It bloats history and cannot be reviewed. It can go stale relative to the source, and it may embed host-specific paths. It is also a supply-chain risk, since the binary cannot be shown to match the source. scripts/check.sh already builds `./cmd/workbench`, so the artifact is redundant.
finding.suggestion: Remove the binary from version control, add `drivers/cogent/workbench` to .gitignore, and produce it in CI or a build step with `go build ./cmd/workbench`.
